To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
eosinophil-fibroblast interactions in the dermal compartment are induced and activated in atopic dermatitis via pruritogenic IL-31 and alarmin IL-3.

IL-31 and/or IL-33 can induce the release of cytokines, chemokines and adhesion molecules from eosinophls and fibroblats through differential intracellular signaling pathways, which may be involved in the pathogenesis of AD.

IL-31 and the alarmin IL-333 synergistically enhance the activation of eosino- and fibroblastic cells in co-culture, and that the differential activation profiles of intracellular signaling molecules are involved in the distinct induction of chemokines and cytokines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the activation of eosino-phil-fibroblastic interaction by IL-31 and/or IL-33 in the pathogenesis of AD.
a novel mechanism of eosinophilotropic cytokine IL-31, and alarmin IL- 33, which might contribute to the pathogenesis in AD.
a better understanding of the role of IL-33 in eosinophil-fibroblastic interaction in AD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the activation of eosino-phils interacting with dermal fibro-blasts by pruritogenic IL-31 and alarmin IL-3 may contribute to the pathogenesis and progression of AD.
IL-31 and/or IL-33 could induce eosinophil and fibroblast activation via the differential activation of signaling pathways.

IL-33, IL-31 and their receptor components are important for the activation of eosino-dermal fibroblastic interaction and the subsequent release of cytokines/chemokines in the inner dermal compartments of AD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
eosinophils, fibroblasts and their interactions play a critical role in AD pathogenesis, which could be modulated by IL-31 and/or IL-33.
IL-31-activated eosinophils interact with IL-33-stimulated fibroblasts to induce a pruritic inflammatory response in AD.
the interaction between eosinophil and fibroblast in the dermis is activated by pruritogenic IL-31 and alarmin IL-333, which would be a potential target for the treatment of pruritic AD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-31 and/or IL-33 may play an important role in eosinophil infiltration and activation in AD.
eosinophils can be activated by IL-33, which has been thought to be a Th2-type alarmin.
IL-31 and/or IL-33 may be potential therapeutic targets to suppress eosinophil activation and eosinophil-fibroblast interaction in AD.
